description.narrative:
Women continue to live in poverty despite undertaking immense amounts of work. Over 70% of the work rural women do in Sub Saharan Africa is unpaid, unrecognised and generally unprofitable. This work is compounded on women by the socio-cultural beliefs ofthe husbands, communities where they live as well as the cultural institutions where they belong. More than 70% of the women in HECA region just like in Africa are engaged in agriculture sector mainly as subsistence smallholder producers either of livestock, fisheries, or crop products. These products are largely consumed at household level and where sold the largest portions if not all profits are claimed by men. Where women participate for instance in the fish value chain, they are involved in activities like cleaning and slaughtering for fishermen thus earning low wages.Yet agriculture has been suggested as having the ability to eradicate rural poverty threetimes faster than any other sector. In addition, if women enjoyed greater benefits from their production activities and conducted agriculture as a business, they would easily earn incomes to eradicate household poverty and enjoyed greater food security.
Furthermore, women are unable to speak out on their issues due to harmful cultural practicesand situations that are a contributing factor totheir being illiterate, fearful of consequences, unexposed and lack opportunities for engaging and holding their duty bearers andpolicy makers accountable for their actions, and promises. Yet development processes such as national budgeting, national planning as well as legislation are key moments which develop tools that have direct impacts on women#s wellbeing. Budgets for example articulate and allocate resources which effect local level developmentsincluding in agriculture; national programmes and policies generally guide local development processes yet women are visibly missing in the processes of designing and implementing these actions thus necessitating the building of women#s capacity to and create opportunities for women to engage in and influence these development processes as they have effects on their wellbeing.
In addition, there are several tools which provide for citizens# participation in the development processes such as African Union#s Agenda 2063: the Maputo protocol on Women#s rights: the Malabo declaration on agricultural transformation all of which call for women to actively engage in development processes and hold their local, national, regional and continental leaders mutually accountable for their actions, results and impact on women#s wellbeing. Thusly, a programme has been designed in the HECA region to enhance women#s access to income generating options; reduce socio-cultural norms which keep women in poverty; capacitatewomen and facilitate their engagement and influence in development processes at local, national, regional and continental level.
